## Root-cause analysis (rebar-debug Phase 1)

**Proven mechanism (runtime-confirmed).** `last_pass.publish`'s 3-attempt CAS
publication loop sleeps on a FIXED, UNJITTERED schedule `(0.1, 0.2)[attempt]`
(`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:343`). Two runtime passes driven
through `publish` with an always-colliding `_cas_advance` produced byte-identical
delay sequences — pass A `[0.1, 0.2]`, pass B `[0.1, 0.2]` (identical). Colliding
reconciler passes therefore wake in lockstep and re-collide (thundering-herd), the
same class baldish (e4a6-545b-36af-456d) fixed for the tickets-push `_cas_backoff`.

**Staleness half is already correct (no defect, confirmed — not "fixed").** In the
same probe the `old_oid` fed to each CAS attempt was the value RE-READ after the
sleep: `['aaa', 'bbb', 'ccc']` (a fresh oid per attempt), proving line 344 re-reads
`old_oid` after `sleeper(...)`. Unlike baldish, there is NO staleness bug here; the
only defect is the missing jitter. (No surprise vs. the ticket's scoping note.)

**Defect legitimacy: `defect`.** The unjittered backoff violates the design invariant
— colliding CAS writers must not wake in lockstep — established by the merged baldish
fix (`push_classify._cas_backoff`, additive jitter) and the Jira DC transport jitter
idiom (`adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py:182`), and by this ticket's AC.

**Defect origin (attribution).** `git log -L 343,343:.../last_pass.py` and
`git blame -w` both name commit `fe5a447061cd` "Add durable bridge status and canary
witness" — a `new file` creation that introduced the unjittered schedule as written
(not a carrier of a moved line). Its `rebar-ticket:` trailer is **b69c-5787-81b8-4052**.
Independently verified (NOT copied from baldish): baldish's origin `ebee`
(freeborn-dizzy-raven) touched `push_classify.py`; this line has a different lineage —
the file was created here with the schedule already unjittered, an incomplete-backoff
plan. Close class → `plan_defect`; `--caused-by=b69c-5787-81b8-4052`.

**Caller-dependency sweep.** The `(0.1, 0.2)` delays are internal to `publish`; the
only readers are `publish_process_result` (internal) and the reconciler entry points
(`__main__`, `snapshot`, bridge commands) — none depends on the exact delay values.
The lone assertion on the exact schedule is the existing integration test
`test_last_pass_cas_retries_exactly_three_times_with_fixed_backoff`, updated in scope.
Only-incidental usage → safe to fix.

**Step-7 sibling sweep — no new siblings.** Class = unjittered backoff between
competing CAS/ref-lock writers. `_ref_lock.py` `_cas_advance` sites (502/537/634/719)
are single-shot (raise on reject, no retry-backoff loop); `access_check` JQL poll and
`retry.py`/`acli_rest.py` are single-client transport/poll retries (same class as the
recorded non-sibling `_TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_SECONDS`); `dispatch_apply_phases`,
`generation`, `resign`, and the Jira-DC 429 branch are already jittered. Parity axis:
`publish` is the single CAS-publish core — no parallel surface with its own backoff.
The previously-recorded non-siblings (`_TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_SECONDS`, `_coordinated_fetch`
/`_FETCH_CAS_BACKOFF_S`, single-shot `_cas_advance`) were re-confirmed and not re-filed.
